52,000 lbs of Anhydrous Ammonia on site (maximum intended inventory). 

3) General Accidental Release Prevention Program and Ammonia Specific Release Prevention
Aurorium Denham Springs, LLC complies with the OSHA Process Safety Management for Highly Hazardous Chemicals (PSM) standard relative to anhydrous ammonia. The facility has programs in place to ensure proper operation and maintenance of process systems. All operators associated with the use of anhydrous ammonia have been trained and are knowledgeable in the safe operation of the system.

The storage tank and piping system at this facility has been designed and constructed using good engineering practices and to conform to industry standards. The system includes ammonia detection devices near the storage tank, an excess-flow emergency shutdown valve located on the main line outside the building and 2 sets of safety relief valves to avert serious system overpressure. A water curtain for ammonia vapor suppression is in place surrounding the ammonia storage tank. A regular inspection of the storage tank, piping system, and mitigation equipment ensures ongoing system integrity.

4) Five Year Accident History
Within the last five years, the facility has had no accidental releases of anhydrous ammonia.

5) Emergency Response Program
In the event of an emergency, Aurorium Denham Springs, LLC. will initiate an evacuation of the facility and notify the proper authorities, including the Livingston Parish Fire District #5 and the Livingston Parish - Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC). The LEPC is involved in the overall Aurorium Denham Springs, LLC emergency planning efforts. Employees are trained to evacuate their respective areas in accordance with OSHA 1910.38(a). The facility is not a responding stationary source.

6) Planned Changes to Improve Safety
The facility plans to implement safety improvements driven by the most recent PHA and compliance audit. These changes include additional instrumentation, improve
ments in mechanical integrity procedures, revisions to the emergency response plan, and additional employee training.
